title: Large U.S. banks face rising G-SIB buffers and tighter excess capital: GS
detail:
Large U.S. banks face rising G-SIB buffers and tighter excess capital: GS
Sam Boughedda
Wed, September 2, 2026 at 11:14 AM PDT 1 min read
GS
JPM
BAC
C-PR
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs believes the largest U.S. banks are likely to moderate capital deployment as regulatory buffers rise for a third consecutive year and excess capital levels shrink.

The bank said in a note Wednesday that it expects lenders to pull back "given that excess capital levels have fallen, G-SIB scores have increased YTD, after also increasing in both 2024 and 2025, and the final details on regulatory capital reform are still pending," analyst Richard Ramsden wrote.

Five of the seven global systemically important banks (JPM, WFC, BAC, C, MS, BNY, STT) have moved up one or more G-SIB buckets so far this year, and Goldman said none of the top five is expected to mitigate scores enough to drop a bucket by year-end.

Ramsden notes that second-quarter G-SIB scores rose 23 basis points quarter over quarter, with the largest increases at JPMorgan, Citigroup and Wells Fargo. JPMorgan is up two buckets year to date and now sits in the 7.0% bucket.

The top seven banks hold an estimated $78 billion of excess capital, but Goldman said that falls to $55 billion in 2027 and $20 billion in 2028 as prior G-SIB increases take effect with a two-year lag. Factoring in higher buffers, excess capital could swing to a $21 billion deficit by 2029.

With bank price-to-tangible-book values at 2.1 times, Goldman sees buybacks as less attractive than balance sheet expansion, assuming a 15% increase in total capital return in 2026.

title: Banks Just Hijacked Crypto’s Original Promise: The Revolution Against Wall Street Is Now Owned by Wall Street
detail:
Banks Just Hijacked Crypto’s Original Promise: The Revolution Against Wall Street Is Now Owned by Wall Street
Rich Duprey

USDT-USD

Quick Read

A 21-bank consortium including Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo plans to launch a dollar-backed stablecoin by 2027, turning blockchain into bank-controlled payment rails.

Banks are launching their own stablecoin to prevent non-bank competitors from pulling deposits out of the traditional financial system.

Crypto-native issuers Tether and Circle now face institutional-scale competition, but bank adoption could expand the total stablecoin market and deepen blockchain liquidity.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Crypto was built around removing financial middlemen. Nearly two decades later, some of the world's biggest financial institutions are preparing to become the middlemen on blockchain. A consortium of 21 banks and financial firms plans to create a new company in the second half of 2026 and launch a U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin in the first half of 2027. 

SWKStock / Shutterstock.com

The group includes Bank of America (NYSE:BAC), Citi (NYSE:C), Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS), Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC), Deutsche Bank (NYSE:DB), UBS (NYSE:UBS), and Fidelity Investments. The irony is hard to miss. The institutions crypto was designed to bypass are now building its payment rails.

Wall Street Is No Longer Watching Crypto

The consortium's announcement, published by Wells Fargo on Sept. 1, represents a major change in strategy. The original group contained 10 banks when the project was announced last October. It has now more than doubled to 21 institutions spanning North America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.

The proposed stablecoin would be pegged 1-to-1 with the U.S. dollar and designed for wholesale, institutional, and retail uses, including cross-border payments and digital-asset settlement. The group also intends to expand into other G7 currencies, with the euro first in line.

title: Bank of America (BAC) Stock May Be 31% Undervalued Despite Stablecoin Plans
detail:
Bank of America (BAC) Stock May Be 31% Undervalued Despite Stablecoin Plans
Bailey Pemberton
Wed, September 2, 2026 at 6:08 AM PDT 6 min read
BAC
DX-Y.NYB
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America stock has delivered a strong 3 year run, yet current valuation checks suggest there may still be a gap between the market price and what an Excess Returns intrinsic value estimate implies. For investors, the key issue is how much weight to place on that potential discount when recent share price moves have been relatively modest.

Bank of America is up 131.3% over the past 3 years, which puts recent short term moves into context as part of a much longer strong period for the stock.

The planned role in a consortium to launch a US dollar stablecoin can support long term fee and payments opportunities. At the same time, ongoing regulatory debates such as the Federal Reserve GSIB capital surcharge revision may limit how much capital the bank can return to shareholders.

With a value score of 3 out of 6, Bank of America shows a mixed picture rather than a clear bargain or clear overvaluation on the broader checks, even though both the Excess Returns intrinsic value estimate and earnings multiples currently screen it as undervalued compared with the share price around US$61.99.

The issue now is whether Bank of America stock still offers enough valuation upside after this multi year run to justify new capital going into the shares.

Spot opportunities that echo Bank of America's valuation story by scanning a curated list of 50 high quality undervalued stocks with solid balance sheets and cash flows.

Is Bank of America a Bargain on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model compares profit on shareholders' equity with the cost of that equity to estimate intrinsic value per share for Bank of America. On this view, the bank's Book Value of $39.34 per share and Stable EPS of $5.50 per share, based on analyst return on equity estimates, support an Excess Return of $2.02 per share over a Cost of Equity of $3.48 per share. That is paired with an Average Return on Equity of 12.70% and a Stable Book Value assumption of $43.31 per share.

Combining these inputs, the Excess Returns model indicates an intrinsic value of about $89.95 per share, which is roughly 31.1% above the recent share price around $61.99, so the stock screens as undervalued within this framework. The planned role in a consortium to launch a US dollar stablecoin provides additional context, because it illustrates why the model assumes Bank of America can continue earning returns above its equity cost over time, even while the market prices the stock at a discount to that stream of excess profits.

On these Excess Returns assumptions, Bank of America stock appears undervalued relative to its current trading price.

title: The hunt for yield is changing how investors trade credit: BofA
detail:
The hunt for yield is changing how investors trade credit: BofA
Sam Boughedda
Wed, September 2, 2026 at 5:45 AM PDT 1 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Bank of America said the ongoing search for income is reshaping credit markets, lifting demand for high-quality bonds while changing the tools investors use to manage risk.

The bank wrote in a note that although sovereign bond yields have risen sharply since March, rates volatility has retraced materially, creating a favorable backdrop for risk assets.

"Elevated yields, coupled with a more stable rates backdrop, are making high-quality credit increasingly attractive and encouraging investors to focus on total returns rather than spread compression alone," strategist Ioannis Angelakis wrote.

BofA highlighted fixed maturity funds as one of the most important structural buyers of credit in recent years, with assets under management now around $130 billion.

By offering yields well above bank deposits, they have drawn household savings into credit and reinforced demand at the front end, though BofA noted their growth has slowed from 2024-25.

Market structure is also said to be evolving. Angelakis stated that the expansion of ETFs and portfolio trading has transformed how investors access credit, with liquidity increasingly sourced through scalable portfolio-based solutions rather than individual bond transactions.

BofA added that CDS indices have become the liquidity hedge of choice, evolving beyond their traditional role into tools for rapid portfolio repositioning when bond execution becomes difficult.

A clear framework has emerged, the bank added, with investors seeking alpha through selective bond selection while relying on CDS indices for beta management and index options for downside protection.

A consortium of 21 financial institutions is planning to form a new firm that will issue a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin in the first half of 2027.

Other members of the group include Wells Fargo, Deutsche Bank, UBS, Santander, Capital One and Fidelity Investments.

The project has expanded considerably from its initial announcement in October 2025, which involved only 10 banks.

Ultimately the group aims to introduce digital currencies connected to other G7 currencies, with a euro version among its goals. The move is a significant shift for Wall Street.

For the most part, stablecoins have been the domain of crypto natives like Tether and Circle. Banks now appear more interested in competing than they do in watching those startups create payment networks around them.

The reserve will back the planned token one-to-one and will run on public blockchains. This could make the project particularly useful for institutional transactions and cross-border payments.

The next test comes in 2027, when investors will see if a stablecoin backed by some of the world's biggest institutions will gain major acceptance.

Whether your investments are in the hedge fund or mutual fund arena, one thing is for sure: it's a good bet that the portfolio managers are fond of many of the same stocks. Goldman Sachs just published its Hedge Fund Trend Monitor and Mutual Fund Fundamentals reports, which analyzed $10 trillion in equity positions at the start of the third quarter of 2026. The report had this to say about the overall performance of the two:

Hedge fund portfolios remain closely tied to the AI trade while mutual funds are underweight the complex. The returns of hedge funds and their most popular holdings have been closely correlated with swings in the AI trade during the last few months. The weight of AI infrastructure stocks in mutual fund portfolios has risen sharply this year. Still, it has failed to keep pace with benchmark weights, leaving mutual funds significantly underweight the complex. Outside of AI, hedge funds and mutual funds generally agree on sector tilts. While hedge funds are not benchmarked, comparing their net sector positions to the Russell 3000 reveals tilts similar to mutual fund portfolios. Both groups carry large overweights in Health Care and large underweights in TMT. The most notable area of disagreement is in the consumer sectors, where hedge funds are overweight in Consumer Discretionary and underweight in Consumer Staples. In contrast, mutual funds hold the opposite tilts.
